messages:
sam: heads up — we're seeing a synchronous reset wave across multiple racks in us-west1 and ap-south1, ~15-20% capacity drop. errors show repeated PCIe AER/fatal + nvlink parity messages, plus Xid31 on many cards.

dana: noticed it about 5m ago, jobs started failing with `GPU lost` and the autoscaler is triggering drains. rolling back a few canaries didn't help.

ryan: stack traces and GPU logs? paste the kernel dmesg snippets and nvidia-smi -q output.

sam: pasted logs in thread: ```[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, pid=98765, GPU=a0b0c0d0
[ 12346.000123] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Uncorrected (Severity: Fatal)
[ 12346.001234] nvlink: NVLINK_BRIDGE_LINK_DOWN on bridge 2
```

anita: interesting — nvlink flapping + AER fatal in parallel suggests link-level hardware/firmware issue rather than a single driver bug. any recent firmware pushes?

sam: we rolled a GPU firmware blob to a small subset last night (firmware v5.3.1 -> v5.4.0) for rack 7 and 9 as part of a throughput test. those racks are the ones with the highest error concentration.

ryan: ok that's a likely lead. can we quickly map resets to firmware version? run `fleet-query --filter "firmware!=5.3.1" --group-by rack` and dump results.

dana: output shows racks 7/9/12 have v5.4.0, all showing higher ECC and AER counts. racks with v5.3.1 look nominal.

oncall-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-0472. Severity: high. Channels: #eng-runtime #eng-infra #incidents.

sre-runbook-bot: Suggested immediate mitigation: 1) Set affected racks to drain and failover traffic. 2) Roll back firmware to v5.3.1 for hot racks if rollback supported. 3) Increase capacity in eu-west and us-east to compensate. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-firmware-rollback

sam: executing staged drain on racks 7 and 9 now: `kubectl cordon node-rack7-* && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node-rack7-*` (doing one rack at a time).

dana: rolling capacity: provisioning extra nodes in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, ETA ~12m for warm-up. I've disabled auto-burst for low-priority training queues to hold capacity.

ryan: coordinate with HW team for a safe firmware rollback. confirm rollback image checksum before flash. If rollback not possible quickly, we should isolate NVSwitch lanes via BIOS toggles per runbook.

anita: also flagging that the nvlink errors generate a lot of telemetry noise — alert thresholds should be adjusted to avoid ACL thrash. making a short-lived suppress on nvlink AER alert noise for affected racks.

sam: after rolling back firmware on rack7 (one host) we saw errors stop on that host within ~90s and a node rejoin. results look promising. rolling rack9 next.

dana: note — cost note: provisioning extra capacity and emergency rollbacks will hit overtime/spot-pricing. logging cost impact under INC-2026-0472.

ryan: postmortem action items: (A) stop-gap: add firmware gating for canaries + automated rollback hook for next deploys, (B) add NVLink and AER rate-limiters to telemetry to avoid surge-triggered mass drains, (C) test full rollback path in staging, (D) add explicit healthcheck to avoid immediate autoscale drains when nvlink-only flaps occur.

sam: agreed. will keep thread updated as racks are rolled back. thanks all. :thumbsup:

anita: putting a tentative postmortem tag on the incident. assign owners: ry an (firmware/rollback), dana (capacity), sam (coordination + runbook updates).

sam: final note — if you see any `Xid 13` correlated with `nvlink` after rollback, ping me immediately; might be a different codepath.
